diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, non-germinal-center B-cell phenotype by Hans algorithm (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive), with a double-expressor IHC profile (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%) and Ki-67 about 80%. Diagnosed on excisional left axillary node biopsy 2026-08-25; flow shows a kappa-restricted CD19+/CD20+/CD10- large B-cell population. This is not breast carcinoma recurrence: lesional cells are CD20 and PAX5 positive and AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative, with no morphologic carcinoma. I treat it as a second, separate malignancy that arose 9.5 years after ER-positive pT2N0 left breast cancer; the breast cancer history does not change lymphoma management. EBER negative. Bone marrow not involved (2026-09-08).
stage: Lugano / Ann Arbor stage III B. Nodal disease is above and below the diaphragm (left axillary, mediastinal, mesenteric, para-aortic), and splenic involvement by multiple FDG-avid nodules is counted as nodal under Lugano. B symptoms are present: fevers to 38.2-38.4 C for about 5 weeks and drenching night sweats; the approximately 3% weight loss does not meet the B criterion on its own. Bulky disease: mesenteric conglomerate 7.5 x 5.1 cm (SUVmax 22.3), which reaches the 7.5 cm threshold used in many protocols but not the 10 cm threshold. Marrow negative. LDH is elevated (510 U/L; reference upper limit not reported). If the splenic nodules were judged extranodal the stage would be IV B, but that would not change the regimen or the IPI.
biology: Non-GCB (Hans) DLBCL with double-expressor IHC status (MYC IHC 45% at or above the 40% threshold; BCL2 IHC 70% at or above the 50% threshold). Not double-hit: interphase FISH on 200 nuclei shows no MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21) or BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement, so no double-hit or triple-hit designation and no double-hit-specific regimen is indicated. Adverse features: non-GCB phenotype, double-expressor status, Ki-67 80%, beta-2-microglobulin 2.9 mg/L (elevated), bulk, B symptoms and elevated LDH. Still outstanding and not needed for first-line decisions: karyotype (tissue was sent for cytogenetics, result not in the export), CD45 stain, gene-expression cell-of-origin, and MYD88 L265P / CD79B status, which matter mainly for trial eligibility.
prognosis: Curative intent. IPI is 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age 59 and ECOG 1 score 0; no more than one extranodal site), which is low-intermediate by IPI and NCCN-IPI. Adverse biology (non-GCB, double-expressor, elevated B2M, bulk, B symptoms) means the real outlook is worse than the IPI alone suggests. The most important factor is that doxorubicin, the most active agent in standard R-CHOP, is not usable here (see first-line treatment). I therefore expect a lower cure rate than the textbook IPI-2 figures for R-CHOP. I will not quote a precise survival number, because the anthracycline-free regimen I recommend has no validated outcome data in this setting. Her long-term outlook will be refined by the end-of-treatment PET result.
first_line_treatment: Decision: no doxorubicin-containing regimen. This excludes R-CHOP, Pola-R-CHP (the NCCN-preferred, POLARIX-eligible option for IPI 2-5), DA-EPOCH-R, and R-CHOP with lenalidomide or ibrutinib. Reasons: (1) LVEF is 45% (biplane), down from 62% in 2016, with GLS -14%, which places her at high risk of anthracycline cardiotoxicity; (2) she already received cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2 (dose-dense AC, 2016) plus left chest radiotherapy and has hypertension; (3) six cycles of doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 would add 300 mg/m2, reaching about 540 mg/m2, at or above the usual lifetime maximum of 450-550 mg/m2 and well beyond the level where prior chest radiotherapy adds risk. Re-challenge is not justified even if LVEF recovers. Preferred plan: enrol in an anthracycline-free or polatuzumab-based trial if one can open within about 2-3 weeks. If not, treat with anthracycline-free rituximab-based chemotherapy: R-CEOP-21 for 6 cycles (rituximab 375 mg/m2 day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 day 1; vincristine 1.4 mg/m2, max 2 mg, day 1; etoposide 100 mg/m2 days 1-3; prednisone 100 mg days 1-5), with doses verified by pharmacy. This is a deliberate departure from NCCN-preferred regimens: NCCN does not list an anthracycline-free preferred first-line option for DLBCL, and R-CEOP evidence is weaker than R-CHOP, but the anthracycline contraindication outweighs that. Cardiac optimisation and the remaining pre-treatment tests run in parallel, not in series, so that treatment starts within about 2-3 weeks. No mediastinal or left-chest radiotherapy. Radiotherapy to residual mesenteric disease is decided after end-of-treatment PET.
cns_risk: No CNS-directed prophylaxis is recommended now. CNS-IPI: elevated LDH scores 1; age 59 (not over 60), ECOG 1 and no adrenal or kidney involvement score 0; extranodal involvement is 0 if the spleen is counted as nodal, or 1 if counted as extranodal. Total 1-2, low-to-intermediate CNS relapse risk. Non-GCB and double-expressor status add concern, but there is no double-hit lymphoma, no testicular, adrenal, kidney, epidural or paraspinal disease, and only one extranodal organ (spleen). I follow NCCN in not recommending intrathecal or high-dose methotrexate prophylaxis. I would revisit this if pathology later shows a double-hit rearrangement, if adrenal, kidney, testicular or epidural disease emerges, or if the CNS-IPI rises to 3 or more. No brain MRI or lumbar puncture is needed unless neurologic symptoms appear; her neurologic exam is non-focal.
response_assessment: Baseline: FDG PET-CT (report undated in export; confirm the date) with SUVmax axillary 17.8, mediastinal 15.4, mesenteric 22.3 (largest mass 7.5 cm), para-aortic 16.9, and splenic nodules 16.2; no brain, marrow or liver involvement. Response assessed by Lugano 2014 criteria with Deauville scoring. Interim PET after cycle 2: Deauville 1-3 means continue; Deauville 4-5 means high-risk, so confirm by biopsy of the most avid site if equivocal and move to a trial or salvage-type approach rather than adding an anthracycline. End-of-treatment PET-CT about 4-6 weeks after cycle 6: complete metabolic response means surveillance; residual PET-avid mass prompts biopsy if equivocal and a decision on involved-site radiotherapy to the mesenteric mass. Laboratory monitoring: CBC with differential, CMP, LDH and uric acid each cycle; beta-2-microglobulin at baseline and end of treatment. Cardiac monitoring: troponin and NT-proBNP each cycle, with echocardiogram with GLS before cycle 1, after cycle 3 and at the end of treatment; cardiac MRI if LVEF does not recover. Breast surveillance continues with annual mammography (last 2026-03, BI-RADS 2).
pretreatment_workup: Repeat before cycle 1, because the labs are from 2026-09-01 and treatment has been pending: CBC with differential, CMP, magnesium, phosphate, LDH with reference range, uric acid, beta-2-microglobulin, PT/aPTT and urinalysis. Cardiology: 12-lead ECG, high-sensitivity troponin, NT-proBNP, repeat transthoracic echo with GLS, and cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement and extracellular volume if the echo does not clarify the cause (anthracycline and radiation injury versus infiltration or myocarditis). Also assess for ischemia, since left breast radiotherapy irradiated the LAD territory and she has uncontrolled hypertension. Pathology: obtain the karyotype result and CD45 stain; send MYD88 L265P and CD79B sequencing only if trial eligibility requires it. Infection: HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs are all nonreactive, so no HBV antiviral prophylaxis is needed for rituximab; she is HBV non-immune, so offer hepatitis B vaccination now, ideally before cycle 1 when response is better. HCV antibody and HIV are nonreactive. Consider VZV serology and TB risk screening if timing allows. Non-live vaccines before chemotherapy where feasible: influenza (October), COVID-19, pneumococcal and recombinant zoster. Baseline neuropathy examination, since she had paclitaxel in 2016 and vincristine is planned. Central venous access placement before cycle 1. No further staging is needed beyond the PET and marrow.
supportive_care: Cardiac: start cardio-oncology co-management now. For asymptomatic LV systolic dysfunction (LVEF 45%) I recommend guideline-directed therapy: an ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI plus an evidence-based beta-blocker, with an SGLT2 inhibitor if cardiology agrees. This also treats her blood pressure (146-148/88-90 on amlodipine alone), with a target below 130/80; amlodipine can continue. Monitor potassium and creatinine, especially with TMP-SMX. Prednisone pulses will raise BP and glucose and cause fluid retention: daily weights, and report edema. Tumor lysis: intermediate risk (bulk 7.5 cm, LDH elevated, Ki-67 80%), with uric acid 5.8 mg/dL on 2026-09-01. Start allopurinol 300 mg daily two days before cycle 1 (febuxostat if intolerant), with hydration and a BMP; use rasburicase only if uric acid is high at presentation or rises, after G6PD testing. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis (pegfilgrastim or biosimilar, or on-body injector) each cycle: prior chemotherapy and radiotherapy are febrile neutropenia risk factors and the regimen carries substantial neutropenic risk. PJP prophylaxis: TMP-SMX throughout the steroid period; her penicillin allergy (childhood hives) is no barrier to TMP-SMX. Routine antibacterial prophylaxis only if ANC is expected below 0.1 for more than 7 days. Antiemetics: NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist and olanzapine, without extra dexamethasone because prednisone is already given. Bowel regimen for vincristine. Fever: she has been taking acetaminophen for fevers, which masks them; she should check temperature before each dose and call for 38.0 C or higher. Neutropenic fever pathway should account for her penicillin allergy history, with allergy assessment for cephalosporin use. Bone: osteopenia (lumbar T-score -1.8 in 2025), so continue calcium and vitamin D and reassess DEXA earlier than 2027 with the bone team, since steroid pulses add bone loss. Anastrozole: continue to the planned completion in November 2026. It does not treat lymphoma, does not interact meaningfully with the regimen, and stopping it abruptly gains nothing; I will inform the breast team. Nutrition and exercise: dietitian review for the 3% weight loss; physiotherapy or a supervised exercise plan to rebuild the activity she has stopped. Psychosocial: social work, work and leave documentation, and caregiver support from her husband.
fitness_and_goals: Fit for curative-intent therapy. She is 59, ECOG 1, NYHA class I, independent, with normal marrow and organ function (eGFR 85; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 84 mL/min at 70.1 kg; LFTs and albumin normal; HIV and HCV nonreactive). The main limit on therapy is cardiac, not general fitness. Her stated goals are cure and return to full-time work. An anthracycline-free regimen can serve both goals, but I will tell her plainly that its cure rate is likely lower than the anthracycline-based standard, and that this trade-off is accepted to avoid a real risk of heart failure. Expect about 4-5 months of therapy with fatigue, neutropenia and infusion days; plan for a leave or a graded return to work. Her questions are answered: the echo result means her heart limits which lymphoma drugs are safe, and anastrozole continues to November 2026. Consent discussion should include her husband, who drives her to visits. Code status and health care proxy are not documented.
